full_judgment: 16. In the light of Mr Sadat's contention that what the defendant/appellant pleaded was not set off as contemplated by Order VIII, rule 6, but simply claim of prior adjustment, before proceeding to address other points, it is pertinent to resolve, at the very incept, the question as to whether a plea of adjustment is distinct from that of set off. Order VIII, rule 6 of the Code Civil Procedure contemplates a defendant to put up a plea of set off, which requires payment of ad valorem Court Fee under the Court Fees Act, if a defendant wishes to whittle or thwart the plaintiffs claim on the ground that the plaintiff also owes him money. The Appellate Division in United Shipping Corporation Ltd vs WH Bennet 36 DLR (AD) 175, proclaimed, amongst others, that the said provision postulates that the claim is to be made at the first hearing unless permitted by the Court, that both the parties must fill the same character as they fill in plaintiffs suit, that the claim demanded to be set off must be legally recoverable from the plaintiff. Claim for set off must not be barred by limitation on the date of the suit. (Narendra vs Tarulal 25 and in the Court Fees Act, CWN 800). Unambiguous language in Order VIII, rule 6 as well as in the Court Fees Act transmit a clear message to the effect that if a defendant, desirous to put forward a claim that the plaintiff also owes him money, fails to hoist a plea of set off, paying required Court Fee, will face cadit question, so far as such a claim in reversal is concerned.
